title: HOLC Grades Houston Neighborhoods
description: The Home Owners' Loan Corporation grades Houston neighborhoods A through D; the Big Ten Academic Alliance catalog dates the Houston sheet 1937. Fifth Ward and Fourth Ward/Freedmen's Town are graded D ("Hazardous"), as is the core of Third Ward around Emancipation Park, while much of Second Ward is left ungraded. Historians find the maps recorded and codified racial judgments that the FHA and private lenders were already applying, rather than causing them on their own.

title: Texas's First Freeway Opens
description: Construction on the Gulf Freeway began in September 1946; its first section, downtown to Telephone Road, opened on September 30, 1948. It reached Galveston in 1952 and became I-45 in 1957. About 1,500 homes were removed for it, mostly in northern Third Ward and Park Place.

title: Eastex and East Freeways Begin
description: The first sections of the Eastex Freeway (US-59 North) and the East Freeway (I-10 East) open. Over the next decade the Eastex splits Frenchtown and western Fifth Ward and runs through Kashmere Gardens.

title: Federal-Aid Highway Act
description: The Federal-Aid Highway Act of 1956 pays 90% of the cost of Interstate construction. Houston's radial freeways, converging on downtown, pass through several Black and Mexican-American neighborhoods near the center, including Fifth Ward and Fourth Ward.

title: Fourth Ward Cut Off From Downtown
description: The Colored Carnegie Library in Fourth Ward, cut off by nearby freeway work, closes in 1961 and is razed in 1962 for the Clay Avenue extension. The downtown segment of I-45, opened as the Pierce Elevated in 1967, separates Freedmen's Town from downtown.

title: Civil Rights Act Passes
description: The Civil Rights Act outlaws discrimination in public accommodations and employment; the Fair Housing Act follows in 1968. By then, freeway routes and decades of lending patterns had already shaped where Houstonians could live.

title: I-10 East Cuts Through Fifth Ward
description: The East Freeway's link to US-59 downtown opens. It runs through southern Fifth Ward parallel to Lyons Avenue and dead-ends Lyons at Harbor Street, ending it as a through route. With the Eastex Freeway, it leaves Fifth Ward bounded by freeways.

title: Petrochemical Growth Along the Ship Channel
description: Refineries and chemical plants that expanded after World War II line the Houston Ship Channel, beside East End neighborhoods such as Manchester and Harrisburg and the city of Galena Park.

title: Loop 610 Nearly Complete
description: The Sidney Sherman Bridge opens on the East Loop; the last I-610 interchange, with I-10 East, is finished in 1976. The loop had been under construction since 1950; on the north side it forms the southern edge of Independence Heights.

title: June 1976 Brays Bayou Flood
description: Heavy rain in June 1976 floods Brays Bayou, damaging the Texas Medical Center, Rice University, the University of Houston and the Museum District.

title: Suburban Growth
description: Houston's suburbs grow rapidly — The Woodlands, Sugar Land, Katy, Pearland — while the city annexes outlying areas such as Clear Lake City (1977) and later Kingwood (1996).

title: Oil Bust
description: Oil prices collapse in 1986, the low point of the 1982–87 oil bust. Houston lost about 211,000 jobs between February 1982 and March 1987.

title: First Toxics Release Inventory Data
description: EPA publishes the first Toxics Release Inventory data (reporting year 1987, required by the 1986 Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act).

title: Houston Is Majority-Minority
description: The 1990 Census counts non-Hispanic whites at 40.6% of Houston's population, down from 62.4% in 1970 — the city became majority-minority during the 1980s.

title: October 1994 Flood
description: Record rain on October 15–19 floods the East and West Forks of the San Jacinto River around Kingwood and Lake Houston. On October 20 ruptured pipelines set the river on fire; at least 17 people die. (Harris County Flood Control District buyouts had begun in 1985.)

title: Tropical Storm Allison
description: Allison drops up to 36.99 inches of rain at the Port of Houston in June 2001 and causes about $9 billion in damage, including about $2 billion to public facilities, especially the Texas Medical Center.

title: Inner-Loop Redevelopment
description: The Heights, Montrose, Midtown, EaDo and Fourth Ward see rapid redevelopment and rising property values, displacing long-time renters in some formerly redlined areas.

title: Memorial Day Flood
description: Storms on May 25–26, 2015 flood more than 6,000 structures in Harris County; Meyerland along Brays Bayou is among the hardest hit.

title: Tax Day Flood
description: The April 17–18, 2016 storm floods about 9,820 structures. Meyerland floods again; it will flood a third time in Harvey, about 27 months after the first.

title: Hurricane Harvey
description: Harvey is the most significant tropical cyclone rainfall event in U.S. history: 60.58 inches near Nederland, and 36–48 inches across much of the Houston area. About 300,000 structures flood across Southeast Texas. EPA reports 13 Superfund sites flooded or possibly damaged, and the cap on the San Jacinto River Waste Pits is damaged.

title: Inequality Persists
description: ACS 2018–22 estimates put median household income at $135,894 in Afton Oaks/River Oaks and $39,893 in Greater Fifth Ward. Life expectancy differs by about 20 years between Harris County ZIP codes. Turn on the income and HOLC layers together to compare today's map with the 1930s grades.
